type: execute, motion, macro, observe or finish.
Only the selected payload is active.
Completed responses are validated before use.
A model “finish” claim cannot set official task success. Stable gripper gap is measured feedback, not object-attachment proof.
Generic fragments handle repeated local control; optional native macros keep their own prerequisites.
Sequence of 1–6 generic segments; at most 240 control steps per grant.
Measured completion and explicit observation checkpoints.
Short numerical pose/gripper target; 1–5 local control steps.
A short grant may end before target arrival.

Its own grounding / calibration / feasibility requirements apply.
One pose-hold step retaining gripper command; finish also makes a model completion claim.
Neither replaces the independent benchmark predicate.
An unavailable macro returns a reason to the model; legacy grasp verification is not a universal gate before direct execution.
Coordinates refer to the robot grip site in world metres; orientation is the hand’s absolute world quaternion (wxyz).
Absolute world xyz target; quaternion_wxyz or null to retain measured entry orientation.
Resolve xyz displacement once from the measured segment-entry pose.
World displacement using the contact profile; a stall is not a contact certificate.
Hold entry pose; open or close as an explicit stage; require pose arrival, minimum duration and stable measured gap.
Hold the entry pose and command for its declared max_steps, then return.
Yield after that segment. Pending stages do not autoplay or resume implicitly after a handoff.
The first descent stalled; the model chose to close at the reached height and inspect a short lift.
Next saved observation (step 195): soup can visibly lifted with the gripper. Attachment is judged from subsequent evidence.
Targets are tracked from measured pose with bounded Cartesian commands.

≤120 steps per segment; ≤240 per execution grant. Arrival needs two stable samples. Gripper stages require at least 8 open or 12 close actions. These local bounds do not impose a task time/action/call limit.
Local measurements determine completion or yield; they do not decide physical task success.
Position and rotation within profile tolerances for 2 consecutive samples; acknowledge completion only after a real action.
At least 8 open / 12 close actions; 5 recent gaps span ≤0.6 mm; pose arrival also required.
After ≥16 actions, error improves by <0.8 mm over 12 samples. Weighted error = position error + 0.05 × rotation error.
Outside set_gripper while maintaining close: gap rises ≥6 mm above its observed minimum for 3 consecutive samples.
observation_after, completed wait, step budget or target-envelope rejection. Pending segments never autoplay.
A stall does not certify contact identity. Pose/gap completion does not certify grasp or placement. Continuation requires a new model decision from current evidence.

No task-wide time, action or call cap. Official success, existing error/conflict paths and user stop remain termination conditions. User stop is handled at the feedback boundary.
The 180-second deadline covers HTTP open and the full SSE response after authentication.
server_is_overloaded with HTTP 503 or absent status: at most 2 overload retries.
Missing completion, truncated event, stream interruption or network error: at most 2 retries in total for this category.
Same observation, no response envelope and no history commit. Partial output is never executed.
Overload and transient counters are separate. Mixed errors can exceed 3 total sends; accepted backoff is at most 60 s.
HTTP 520 / unknown_error and deadline exceeded do not retry. A new full attempt needs new approval and output.
No model downgrade or API-key fallback. t0/t1 recorded zero request errors and zero retries.
The runner stops at official success; physical truth examines the state at that same boundary.
task_success / libero_success use the original task predicate; an object may still be held.
Physical checks at termination: containment, release, support and rest. Rest uses the recent 10-step displacement/rotation window when available.
38 diagnostic actions: 10 open + 8 lift + 20 settle. Inspect possible release/settle effects separately.
raw_terminal AND [strict_terminal OR (hold_only AND strict_after AND raw_after)]. Read the saved frozen result; do not rescore a diagnostic pass.
Hold-only: each failing atom has only permitted hold/rest/orientation failures and also fails not_held or robot_not_touching_part. Support/below-rim failures are excluded.
Report official completion time only when official success and completion_time_eligible are true.
Time includes model wait, control computation, simulator actions and logging; excludes setup, planning, approval and post-stop diagnosis. It is not video playback length.

Two single attempts on custom layouts. Both plans have regions=[]; they do not test directional-region behavior.

Required preparation settings: --reasoning-effort high --planning-video --request-deadline-s 180 --stream-progress; official episode index 0, verified custom state and observation hash. Use the protocol’s environment and simulator Python. The runner config selects Astra; there is no --model flag.
The exact executable templates are in [P §5]. start --auto-approve also executes; it is not a preparation command.
